Personality: Mithridates, a prominent figure of the Mithridatids, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Mithridates owes allegiance to the Kingdom of Pontus, hailing from the noble house of Mithridatids. Historical Record: Mithridates III, king of Pontus, of a Persian noble house that claims kinship with the Achaemenids. His sisters are married to Antiochus III and to the rebel Achaios, so Pontus has a foot in both camps of the Seleucid quarrel. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
